description.narrative: The development objective of the Productive Safety Net Project for Ghana is to support the Government to strengthen safety net systems that improve the productivity of the poor. This project has consist of the following five components. First component, productive inclusion is to support productive inclusion activities for extremely poor households in targeted communities. Second component, labor intensive public works (LIPW) program is to extend income-earning opportunities to poor households through LIPW, which maintain or rehabilitate assets that improve the productivity of communities and respond to the anticipated effects of climate change; Third component, livelihood empowerment against poverty (LEAP) cash transfers is to smooth consumption among extremely poor households.Fourth component, social protection systems strengthening is to strengthen SP delivery systems to improve the efficiency, effectiveness and transparency of safety net interventions through (i) assisting Ghana National Household Registry (GNHR) in its collection of quality household data in targeted regions; (ii) designing and rolling out a single window citizen engagement service (SWCES); and (iii) providing technical assistance for strengthening the monitoring and evaluation (M and E) framework and system, including an impact evaluation for the project and development of an management information system (MIS).
To support the Government to strengthen safety net systems that improve the productivity of the poor.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: <p>Target was formally revised and documented in the July 2020 Restructuring Paper. However, the 107,574 beneficiaries targeted during COVID-19 were not reflected in the final results framework.</p>

title.narrative: LIPW sub-projects with operations and maintenance arrangements in place

comment.narrative: <p>100 percent of LIPW subprojects had operations and maintenance plans at project closing against a target of 85 percent. Furthermore, Facility Management Committees (FMCs) had been formed in all subproject communities, and trainings for the FMCs had been conducted. These FMCs ensure sustainability of the community assets developed under the project.</p>

<p>The project achieved 100 percent of its target as all beneficiaries of the PI, LIPW and LEAP programs owned bank accounts through the project.</p>

<p>Note that:</p>

<p>(1). Beneficiaries with E-zwich cards are considered as Bank Account holders;</p>

<p>(2). Targeted beneficiaries do not have Accounts until enrolled. Therefore all enrolled beneficiaries for the 3 programs are paid trough E-zwich and considered to have Bank Accounts.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of beneficiaries with a bank account

comment.narrative: <p>This is not a PDO indicator and was entered in error as such and could not be removed from the ICR data sheet. It, however, is an intermediate indicator referring to: PI, LIPW, LEAP. All enrolled beneficiaries for the 3 programs are paid through E-zwich and considered to have Bank Accounts. That makes it 100 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Average annual earnings of unskilled workers in LIPWs (cedi)

comment.narrative: <p>The project achieved an average of GHS 1,078.56 in annual earnings exceeding its target of GHS 600 by unskilled LIPW workers. The figure represents the average achieved over the period 2020 – 2021 where full years of implementation are obtained.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries receiving a start-up grant under the CLASS subcomponent

comment.narrative: <p>The project was able to exceed this target by enrolling 20,085 beneficiaries who received start-up grants under the CLASS subcomponent against a target of 15,000. Restructuring necessitated by the combined impact of the partial withdrawal of Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) Trust Fund amounting to US$7.45 million (as a result of the negative economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the UK) in May 2021 and inflation in April 2022 resulted in reduced project funding. This notwithstanding, the project overachieved this intended end target through program implementation efficiency gains achieved with the help of digitized tools and leveraging existing government structures and resources particularly at the decentralized level, among others.   </p>

<p>20,351 beneficiaries received entrepreneurship training against a target of 15,000. Restructuring necessitated by the combined impact of the partial withdrawal of Foreign Commonwealth and Development Office (FCDO) Trust Fund amounting to US$7.45 million (as a result of the negative economic impact of the COVID-19 pandemic on the UK) in May 2021 and inflation in April 2022 resulted in reduced project funding. This notwithstanding, the project exceeded this indicator’s end target through program implementation efficiency gains.</p>

title.narrative: Beneficiaries of social safety net programs

comment.narrative: <p>The LIPW program achieved 115 percent of its beneficiary target (34,579 against 30,000 targeted beneficiaries). This represents all beneficiaries who have ever worked at the LIPW sites and received payment.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of LIPW payments and LEAP grants made on time to beneficiaires

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator achieved only 47 percent of its intended end target of 75 percent, primarily due to delays in disbursements of cash transfer funds to the LEAP program. This in turn was due to the dire macro fiscal situation in the country which led to overall delays in government disbursements, and delayed roll over to an electronic MIS for LIPW, which meant that gathering data at the decentralized level was slow. For LIPW, allowable time lapse is 15 calendar days between conclusion of work and payment as stated in the POM. According to project reporting, there were 698 payments made within 15 days over the total number of 5,735 payments, which amounts to 12.2 percent. LEAP operates on a bi-monthly payment schedule with predetermined payment dates indicated on the LEAP calendar. All payments made on the stated dates on the calendar are considered payments made on time. LEAP recorded 100 percent on time paymets in 2019; 49 percent in 2020; 83.3 percent in year 2021 and 0 percent in2022. On average, 58.1 percent of payments were made on time. To derive the overall score for PDOI-5, the Project took a simple average to get 35.1 percent against the target of 75 percent.</p>

title.narrative: LEAP Beneficiaires selected using the GNHR

comment.narrative:
<p>62 percent (against a target of 75 percent) of LEAP beneficiaries were selected through the GNHR during the lifetime of the project.  Total number of LEAP beneficiary households over GPSNP = 196,740, of which:</p>

<ul>
 <li>89,166 were selected during the regular course of the program, and </li>
 <li>107,574 were enrolled and paid one-time COVID-19 transfers in 2020</li>
</ul>

<p>Among these, 120,988 or 61.5 percent were selected using GNHR.</p>

<p><em>Note</em>: The remaining 38.5 percent of beneficiaries who were not targeted through GNHR are those who had been targeted by LEAP prior to GNHR’s initiation. These remaining were also targeted using categorical and PMT targeting.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of beneficiaries who are identified as extremely poor according to targeting criteria

comment.narrative: <p>The project recorded an achievement of 77 percent against a target of 70 percent. Given that GNHR had not yet reached all program areas to verify poverty status, the ICR looked to other sources to determine the efficacy of this PDO indicator. There were 89,166 LEAP households enrolled onto the main (non-COVID) LEAP program; and 107,574 selected using GNHR during COVID-19. Of the 89,166, a total of 13,414 of the households were deemed to be extreme poor according to GNHR’s household poverty classification. The poverty status of the rest (75,752) could not be determined. As such, for this group the ICR assigns the Social Protection Public Expenditure Review (SP PER)’s estimated 37 percent extreme poverty rate. For the COVID-19 LEAP households, it is assumed that all were extremely poor since they were the most vulnerable as determined by GNHR. The extreme poverty rate for LIPW is assumed to equal that determined in the 2016 LIPW impact evaluation, i.e., 86.9 percent. Taking a weighted average of these rates yields an estimated extreme poverty rate of 77.4 percent.</p>

title.narrative: Percentage of beneficiaries of the LEAP Program enrolled onto the NHIS

comment.narrative: <p>79 percent (against a target of 90 percent) of LEAP beneficiaries were enrolled on the NHIS at project closing. This, however, is likely an underestimate since there were some beneficiaries already on NHIS but not enrolled by the LEAP Management Secretariat, and therefore were not included in this count.</p>

title.narrative: LIPW beneficiaries participating for two consecutive years

comment.narrative: <p>29, 644 out of 34,578 beneficiaries (or approximately 86 percent) had the opportunity to work for two or more years under the LIPW program. This target was set with the goal of deepening the impacts of the project by providing beneficiaries with a longer working opportunity. Exceeding this target means that more beneficiaries received higher wages helping them weather the multiple crises (especially high inflation) over the duration of the project.</p>

title.narrative: Grievance cases resolved through the Single Window Citizen Engagement Service within the stipulated timeframe (disaggregated by gender)

comment.narrative: <p>Overall, the SWCES achieved 94 percent timely grievance resolution rate against a target of 75 percent. The stipulated timeframe based on the PAD is 3 weeks after case is lodged in the system. Values derived are generated by the system based on the basic calcuation of number of cases resolved out of the number lodged within the period. This is automatically obtained from the system.</p>

title.narrative: Percent of beneficiaires who initiated or expanded a household enterprise

comment.narrative: <p>This indicator exceeded its target by 25.7 percentage points with 95.7 percent of beneficiaries initiating or expanding a household enterprise against the operation’s target of 70 percent. Data  shows that 19,179 beneficiaries received <u>both</u> tranche 1 and tranche 2 while 20,037 received only tranche1</p>

title.narrative: Percent of respondents reporting that the assets (sub-projects) created through LIPW improved their livelihoods

comment.narrative: <p>98 percent (against a target of 70 percent) of beneficiaries reported an improvement in their livelihoods thanks to LIPW sub-projects. This represents 140 percent achievement of the target. The estimate is based on respondents’ assessment of improvements in their livelihoods since the completion of project.  (Source: GPSNP LIPW Performance Evaluation, 2022).</p>

title.narrative: Regions that have data collected on poor households through the GNHR

comment.narrative: <p>GNHR achieved 30 percent of its target. Data collection for only one region was completed within the project implementation period, with  two (2) other regions –Volta and Central, having about 70 percent completion rate at project closing.  </p>

title.narrative: Social Protection Monitoring and Evaluation System established and functional

comment.narrative: <p>The Social Protection Monitoring and Evaluation System was established and functional at project close.</p>

title.narrative: Single Window Citizen Engagement Service System established and fully functional

comment.narrative: <p>The Single Window Citizen Engagement Service (SWCES) system was established and fully functional at project closing. SWCES serves as a one-stop shop for receipt of complaints and resolution for social protection and gender-related issues.</p>

title.narrative: LEAP and LIPW beneficiaries in areas where GCAP and/or Government-led agriculture projects operate referred to agricultural activities

comment.narrative: <p>At project closing, 15,926 persons from LEAP and LIPW households had been linked to Planting for Export and Rural Development (PERD), a government-led agricultural intervention. This represented 43 percent achievement against a target of 30 percent. The beneficiaries had also been provided with assorted seedlings with accompanying agriculture extension support. Prior to the third restructuring in 2022, the indicator was limited to referral of beneficiaries to the Ghana Commercial Agriculture project (GCAP). The project however expanded this indicator through the April 2022 restructuring to enable referrals and linkages of LEAP and LIPW beneficiaries to government-led agriculture interventions.  End target and measurement methods remained the same. </p>
